verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents a first-party auto-shutdown feature for Machines. It places a machine in a stop state after a configurable idle period of one hour to one week, and Linux machines shut down after that idle time even when users are connected. That directly guards against a forgotten instance running up a bill, which satisfies the 'timers or spend limits' story. Missing for 10: any documented spend limits or budget caps, evidence that auto-shutdown can be set via the API or CLI, and independent or hands-on corroboration that it works reliably.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can set auto-shutdown timers or spend limits so a forgotten instance can't silently run up a huge bill

citations.quote: The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity, which can range from one hour to one week.
Linux-based machines shut down after the specified idle time, regardless of whether any users are connected.
